answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may vote on trades or earn reputation. Votes are weighted by stake, and provable fraud—such as endorsing a trade the agent never completed—slashes the bond and removes its influence. This does not make sybils impossible: an attacker can create many, but must fund each one, so splitting a stake across hollow identities adds no voting weight. An atlas of agents may track trust, while nectar rewards honest participation.
